tool.name: WMTS_to_GeoPackage

param.name: wmts_url
param.dialogReference:
URL pointing to the WMTS capabilities document (WMTSCapabilities.xml).

For example: https://services.arcgisonline.com/arcgis/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/WMTS/1.0.0/WMTSCapabilities.xml
param.pythonReference:
URL pointing to the WMTS capabilities document (WMTSCapabilities.xml).

For example: https://services.arcgisonline.com/arcgis/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/WMTS/1.0.0/WMTSCapabilities.xml

param.name: wmts_layer
param.dialogReference:
Layer identifier parsed from the capabilities file. This should pull through from the dropdown once the WMTS Capabilities URL is entered.

The tool only works with EPSG 3857 (Web Mercator).

Example: World_Imagery
param.pythonReference:
Layer identifier parsed from the capabilities file. This should pull through from the dropdown once the WMTS Capabilities URL is entered.

The tool only works with EPSG 3857 (Web Mercator).

Example: World_Imagery

param.name: extent_fc
param.dialogReference:
Polygon feature class or shapefile defining the geographic area to download.

This must be in EPSG 3857.

The polygon feature class must be selected by clicking the folder icon in the tool.
param.pythonReference:
Polygon feature class or shapefile defining the geographic area to download.

This must be in EPSG 3857.

The polygon feature class must be selected by clicking the folder icon in the tool.

param.name: crop_to_extent
param.displayname: Crop Metadata Extent to Input Area
param.dialogReference:
Tick box to clip the output GeoPackage to the exact geometry of the Extent Feature Class. Checked by default.

If unticked, this caches all tiles that intersect with the Extent Feature Class.

For example, without clipping, at level 0 the whole world will be cached as it is 1 tile. With clipping on, the level 0 tile will be clipped to the Extent Feature Class.
param.pythonReference:
Tick box to clip the output GeoPackage to the exact geometry of the Extent Feature Class. Checked by default.

If unticked, this caches all tiles that intersect with the Extent Feature Class.

For example, without clipping, at level 0 the whole world will be cached as it is 1 tile. With clipping on, the level 0 tile will be clipped to the Extent Feature Class.

param.name: min_zoom
param.dialogReference:
Lowest zoom level to download (0-19).

Lower zoom = fewer tiles.
param.pythonReference:
Lowest zoom level to download (0-19).

Lower zoom = fewer tiles.

param.name: max_zoom
param.dialogReference:
Highest zoom level to download (0-19).

Higher zoom = more tiles, larger GeoPackage. Each extra zoom level makes the file roughly four times larger.
param.pythonReference:
Highest zoom level to download (0-19).

Higher zoom = more tiles, larger GeoPackage. Each extra zoom level makes the file roughly four times larger.

param.name: output_gpkg
param.dialogReference: Path and name of the GeoPackage file (.gpkg) to create. An existing file with the same name is overwritten.
param.pythonReference: Path and name of the GeoPackage file (.gpkg) to create. An existing file with the same name is overwritten.

tool.summary:
Downloads tiles from a WMTS service and packages them into an OGC GeoPackage (.gpkg) tile file suitable for offline use in applications such as ArcGIS Pro, ATAK/WinTAK, QGIS and SITAWARE.

Supports WMTS Capabilities parsing, GoogleMapsCompatible tile matrix sets (EPSG:3857 only), retry logic for unstable servers, high-zoom tile extraction, and reads tile size and image format from the WMTS capabilities. Tested with Esri World Imagery, GeoServer WMTS, MapProxy WMTS and RBT WMTS.
tool.usage:
Do NOT use ArcGIS geoprocessing environments with this tool. The tool manages its own workspace, projection, and tile maths.

The Extent Feature Class must be in EPSG 3857 (Web Mercator). If you see NaN tile math errors, define or project the extent to EPSG:3857.

Server errors such as 502s and DNS failures are retried automatically.
